page.layout: One page of text: running head at top; a heading with its number; a woodcut illustration of two men at barrels; a verse emblem with a large initial below the picture; a catchword-like word "Vipera" at the lower right.

main_text.head: Alius vas plenum, alius vacuum replentes. XXVII.
main_text.p: [Woodcut illustration: two men at barrels, one pouring from a jug, the other drawing from a barrel; no text.]
CEu Vacuum facilis Vas est implere laboris, Quod Vero est plenum Velle replere furor:
main_text.l: Sic cuius diuina animum sapientia coepit,
Et Vita inuasit quem melioris amor.
Aut Vacuam humanis, homo, mentem sensibus adfer.

page.notes: The large initial "C" of the verse is a woodcut letter; read as "C" with [?] for the doubtful first letter: C[?]eu. The verse uses long s throughout, transcribed as s. The word "Vipera" at the foot may be a catchword or signature of the emblem; it is set apart at lower right.
